articles.title: Pittsburgh vs Florida State: Panthers Defense Battles, Falls 16-10 at Home
articles.matchup: Final: Florida State Seminoles (5-5) 16, Pittsburgh Panthers (6-4) 10, Fri., Nov. 13, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: at Louisville, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville
articles.text:
Yinz, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it. Florida State 16, Pittsburgh 10 on Friday night at Acrisure Stadium, and the Panthers are 6-4. There were 45,734 of us bundled up on the North Shore, and we deserved a happier walk home across the river.

The defense showed up, I'll give 'em that. Florida State managed 260 yards, ran for just 97 on 33 carries and converted 3 of 13 third downs. Cruce Brookins was everywhere with 10 tackles. Braylan Lovelace forced a fumble and had a tackle and a half for loss. Early in the fourth, Alex Sanford Jr. knocked the ball loose from Ashton Daniels and Shawn Lee Jr. fell on it at our 6 to keep it a 13-10 game.

Our lone touchdown was a beauty. Corey Dailey moved us 85 yards in 10 plays late in the second quarter, hit Malik Knight for 28 deep down the left side and found Ja'Kyrian Turner for an 11-yard score to put us up 7-6 at the half. Turner finished with seven catches.

Then came the play that stung. On our second snap of the third quarter, a throw was intercepted at our 39, and five plays later Florida State was in the end zone. Antonio Chadha's 34-yard field goal pulled us to 13-10, but their kicker answered from 47 with 6:27 left.

We had our chances. Three times we went for it on fourth down and came up short, including a sack near midfield with 8:44 left. After a 64-yard punt pinned us at our own 2 with 1:49 to go, Dailey took off for 24 yards on the first snap and got us to their 48, but the last fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 43 seconds left. Dailey ran for 58 yards on nine carries and battled every snap.

Pittsburgh doesn't do quit. We're still 6-4, still 5-2 at home, and cold November football is our kind of weather. Three rivers, one city, and a whole lot of fight left in this bunch.

Next: at Louisville, Saturday, Nov. 21, kickoff time to be announced. Wear the blue and gold, make some noise on the road, and let's bring one home. Hail to Pitt.

articles.title: Florida State vs Pittsburgh: Panikowski and a Stingy Defense Win 16-10
articles.byline: Gianna Ravello, The Florida State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Florida State Seminoles (5-5) 16, Pittsburgh Panthers (6-4) 10, Fri., Nov. 13, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: vs NC State, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee
articles.text:
Garnet and gold just froze out Pittsburgh. Florida State 16, Pittsburgh 10 on Friday night at Acrisure Stadium, and the Seminoles are 5-5. I packed my one Tallahassee sweater for a November night on the North Shore, and I would wear it every week for wins like this.

Gabe Panikowski was the coolest man in western Pennsylvania. He hit from 37 and 27 yards in the first half, then drilled a 47-yarder with 6:27 left to make it 16-10. Three tries, three makes. Somebody put that young man's right leg in a museum.

The turning point came on Pittsburgh's second snap of the third quarter. We trailed 7-6 at the half, and Rylan Kennedy jumped a throw at the Pitt 39 and brought it back to the 32. Amari Thomas ripped off 16 yards on the very next play, and five snaps after the takeaway, Thomas punched it in from a yard out. 13-7, Noles, and I was hollering in a sea of Pitt gold.

Ashton Daniels kept the offense steady, going 16 of 24 for 163 yards with no interceptions. Jasen Lopez caught five balls for 72 yards, including a 46-yard grab down the left side that set up our second field goal.

But this one belongs to the defense. Pittsburgh converted 5 of 15 third downs and came up empty on three different fourth downs. Caleb LaVallee sacked Corey Dailey on fourth down near midfield with 8:44 left. Then Daniel Hughes boomed a 64-yard punt that pinned Pitt at its own 2 with 1:49 to go, and Charles Lester III broke up a deep ball on that last drive before the final fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 43 seconds left. Chris Jones led us with seven tackles, and CJ Richard Jr. and Ashlynd Barker had six apiece.

It wasn't pretty everywhere. We ran for 97 yards on 33 carries and lost a fumble at their 12 early in the fourth. A road win in Pittsburgh in November is a road win, though, and I will take gritty and happy every single time.

Next: NC State comes to Doak Campbell Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 3:30 PM ET. Sweater off, sunscreen on. Tallahassee, get loud.

articles.title: New York Giants vs Washington Commanders Week 10: 57 Seconds From a Win, 21-24
articles.matchup: Final: Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 24, New York Giants (5-3-1) 21, Thu., Nov. 12, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford. Next: vs Jacksonville Jaguars, Sun., Nov. 22, 4:25 PM ET, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford
articles.text:
Fifty-seven seconds. That's how close we were. Washington 24, New York 21 on Thursday night at MetLife Stadium, and 80,450 of us walked out to the parking lots stunned. We're 5-3-1 and still sitting first in the NFC East, but this one is going to sting all weekend.

Cam Skattebo ran like a man who'd been insulted. He capped a 16-play, 72-yard drive with a 1-yard plunge in the second quarter and bounced in from 13 in the third for a 14-10 lead. Two touchdowns and 78 yards on 18 carries, and every one of them hurt somebody.

Isaiah Likely was the best player on the field. Nine catches, 127 yards, and on third-and-7 from our 34 he ran right through the middle of their defense for a 66-yard touchdown. 21-17 Giants with 8:13 left. J.J. McCarthy finished 23 of 36 for 293 yards.

And the secondary went to work. Jevon Holland intercepted Jayden Daniels at our 2, and Ar'Darius Washington took another one away on fourth down at their 46 with 2:19 to go. Arvell Reese made 13 tackles, Micah McFadden had 10, and Shelby Harris sacked Daniels for a 14-yard loss in the third quarter.

Then the last two minutes. Our punt from their 41 went just 12 yards. A 33-yard interference flag put Washington in business, and Stefon Diggs caught a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. We still had a chance, but McCarthy's deep throw for Malik Nabers was intercepted at their 11.

A few leftovers will keep me up tonight. Dominic Zvada missed a 33-yarder wide left in the first quarter, and Nabers lost a fumble inside their 20 in the third. Those are points left on the field in a three-point game.

Next: the Jacksonville Jaguars at MetLife on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 PM ET. First place is still ours. Let's go keep it. Go Big Blue.

articles.title: Washington Commanders vs New York Giants Week 10: Diggs With 57 Seconds Left, 24-21
articles.matchup: Final: Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 24, New York Giants (5-3-1) 21, Thu., Nov. 12, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford. Next: vs Cincinnati Bengals, Mon., Nov. 23, 8:15 PM ET, Northwest Stadium, Landover
articles.text:
Hail to the Commanders, and somebody please check on my voice. Washington 24, New York 21 on Thursday night at MetLife Stadium, and we took this one in front of 80,450 people who wanted any other ending. We're 3-5-1, and that last minute felt like a whole season.

It was a slugfest for a half. Drew Stevens opened the scoring from 46 yards. The Giants answered with a 16-play march that ate 7:48 and ended with a Cam Skattebo plunge, but Jayden Daniels took us 67 yards in nine plays and flipped it to Ben Sinnott from a yard out with five seconds left in the half. 10-7, us.

Skattebo scored again from 13 early in the third to put them ahead 14-10. Daniels answered on third-and-1, hitting Antonio Williams for a 31-yard touchdown. 17-14. Then Frankie Luvu punched the ball loose from Malik Nabers inside our 20, and Jeremy Reaves fell on it. Reaves had nine tackles and was everywhere all night.

The fourth quarter tried to break my heart. We came up empty on fourth-and-1 at their 30. Isaiah Likely took a catch 66 yards to give New York a 21-17 lead with 8:13 left. Daniels got intercepted twice, once at their 2 by Jevon Holland and once on fourth down by Ar'Darius Washington. I sat down. I stood up. I sat down again.

Then their punt from our 41 went 12 yards and out of bounds, and we had it at our 29 with 1:46 to go. A 33-yard interference flag got us moving, and on third-and-4 Daniels found Stefon Diggs down the middle for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. Three plays, 71 yards, 49 seconds. Rasul Douglas sealed it by intercepting J.J. McCarthy at our 11 with 34 seconds left.

Daniels finished 23 of 33 for 249 yards and three touchdowns. Diggs caught six for 83. Sonny Styles made 13 tackles, Odafe Oweh had a sack, and Tress Way averaged 49.5 yards on four punts. That tie with these same Giants back in October at Northwest Stadium? Consider it settled.

Next up: the Cincinnati Bengals at Northwest Stadium on Monday, Nov. 23, 8:15 PM ET. Rest up, fellas. HTTR.

articles.title: South Florida vs Memphis: The Bulls Climb Out of a 21-0 Hole and Fall Short 52-41
articles.byline: Reina Valdés-Kowalski, The South Florida Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Memphis Tigers (8-2) 52, South Florida Bulls (6-4) 41, Thu., Nov. 12, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa. Next: at Florida Atlantic, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton
articles.text:
I'm hoarse, I'm heartbroken, and I'm proud of this team. Memphis 52, South Florida 41 at Raymond James Stadium on Thursday night, and the Bulls are 6-4. That one hurts, but nobody in green and gold quit.

The first quarter was a nightmare. Memphis scored three times, a fumble at our 21 handed them the third one, and we trailed 21-0 before the first quarter ended. Lots of teams fold right there. Not ours.

Luke Kromenhoek put this whole team on his back. He ran 30 times for 146 yards, threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns, and never threw an interception. Mudia Reuben caught two of those scores, a 3-yarder on fourth down and a 19-yarder with 49 seconds left in the half, and finished with six catches for 98 yards. We went into the locker room down 28-17 and alive again.

The third quarter was pure Tampa thunder. Jason Collins Jr. caught a 13-yard touchdown, then answered a Memphis score on the very next snap with a 75-yard run up the middle. Kromenhoek ran in from 23 to tie it 38-38. Nico Gramatica, perfect on two field goals and five extra points, hit from 38 to give us a 41-38 lead with 8:04 left. Herlin Perry Jr. broke up a Stokes pass at our 8 to force a field goal.

Then it slipped away. Memphis hit a 76-yarder two plays later, and our drive to answer reached their 4 before a fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 3:38 left. Seven sacks were the other story, and that front got to Kromenhoek again on our last real chance.

Look at what this team did, though. We gained 552 yards with 29 first downs, held the ball for 37:35 and converted five of eight fourth downs. Israel Boyce had a sack, and Joshua Porter set up a field goal with a 36-yard punt return.

Next: at Florida Atlantic, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, in Boca Raton. Bring that same fire down to Boca, Bulls. I'll be there, loud as ever.

articles.title: Memphis vs South Florida: Marcus Stokes Has a Hand in Five Scores and the Tigers Go to 8-2
articles.matchup: Final: Memphis Tigers (8-2) 52, South Florida Bulls (6-4) 41, Thu., Nov. 12, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa. Next: at Navy, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis
articles.text:
Somebody bring Tampa a mop. Memphis 52, South Florida 41 on Thursday night at Raymond James Stadium, and the Tigers are 8-2. I flew down expecting a fight, and brother, we got one.

It opened like a parade. Marcus Stokes kept it up the middle on our first drive and outran the whole Bulls secondary to the end zone. Then he found Hunter Tipton from 7 yards. Then Jabari Ishmael jumped on a South Florida fumble at their 21, and four plays later Stokes ran it in from 8. Memphis 21, South Florida 0, and the first quarter hadn't even ended.

Then those Bulls got up off the mat. Luke Kromenhoek ran 30 times and threw for three scores, Jason Collins Jr. went 75 yards on one snap, and by late in the third it was 38-38. With 8:04 left, Nico Gramatica put them ahead 41-38. My heart was somewhere in Hillsborough County.

Two snaps. That's all it took. Stokes dropped back from our 24 and launched one deep right to Jemyri Davis, who caught it in stride and was gone. 76 yards. 45-41. Davis finished with five catches for 161 yards, and I may name my next dog after him.

And then the defense won it. South Florida drove to our 4 and went for it on fourth down, and the throw fell incomplete with 3:38 to go. They got the ball back one more time, and J'Mond Tapp and Elijah Kinsler chased Kromenhoek all around the backfield until it died on fourth-and-27. Jaylin Carter then broke a 26-yard run for the clincher with 44 seconds left. Carter finished with 109 yards and two scores on 21 carries.

Stokes went 15 of 31 for 313 yards and three touchdowns with zero interceptions, and he added 73 yards and two more scores on the ground. That's a hand in five touchdowns. We piled up 581 yards with zero turnovers. Our front had seven sacks, with Tapp at two and a half and Kinsler at two. Mike Montgomery made 19 tackles, which I believe is every tackle available in the state of Florida.

Next stop is Navy, Saturday, Nov. 21, at noon ET in Annapolis. Pack the parkas. Eight wins and counting, and I'm not done hollering.

articles.text:
Somebody tell Lafayette to warm up the boudin, because the Ragin' Cajuns are coming home happy. Louisiana 42, UL Monroe 21 on Thursday night at Malone Stadium in Monroe, and we are 7-3. I drove up from Acadiana with a full voice, and I'm driving home with none.

For one half, those Warhawks made me sweat. They opened with a 15-play march that ate 8:18 off the clock, and Austin Carlisle pushed in from a yard out. Lunch Winfield answered with a 13-yard strike to Shelton Sampson Jr., ULM went back ahead 14-7, and then KeDarius Wade slipped in from 8 yards with 40 seconds left in the half to tie it. Kody Jackson intercepted a throw at our 13 five seconds before the break, and I hugged a complete stranger.

Then our defense took charge of the whole parish. Early in the third, Micah Johnson scooped up a Warhawks fumble and rumbled 18 yards to the end zone for a 21-14 lead. A few series later, Maurion Eleam punched the ball loose, Johnson fell on it at the ULM 19, and JJ Garner went 19 yards on the very next snap. 28-14, and the Cajun side of the stadium was dancing.

Garner was the lightning all night. Nine carries, 104 yards, two scores, including an 18-yarder early in the fourth that made it 35-14. Steven Blanco was the thunder, with 113 yards on 15 carries. After ULM answered to make it 35-21, Blanco carried on all six snaps of a 50-yard drive, had a score wiped out by a flag, shrugged, and walked in from 2 yards anyway with 1:57 left.

We ran for 274 yards on 33 carries and gave the ball away zero times. One Warhawks fumble went the other way for six, and another turned into six more on the next snap. Jake St. Andre made 14 tackles, Collin Jacob made nine, and Johnson had nine to go with that touchdown.

Credit to Monroe, though. Those Warhawks ran it right at us, held the ball for 35:27 and kept swinging into the fourth quarter. Bryson Roland and Carlisle both cleared 100 yards on the ground. But the bragging rights ride back down to Acadiana with us tonight.

Next up, Coastal Carolina visits Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium in Lafayette on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 3:00 PM ET. Come hungry, come loud, and wear that vermilion. Seven wins, and the gumbo is still simmering.

articles.title: UMass vs Toledo: Shut Out at the Glass Bowl, but Timmy Hinspeter Never Stopped Hitting
articles.matchup: Final: Massachusetts Minutemen (5-5) 0, Toledo Rockets (8-2) 24, Wed., Nov. 11, Glass Bowl, Toledo. Next: vs Akron, Wed., Nov. 18, 7:00 PM ET, Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium, Amherst
articles.text:
Some nights you write in the diary, and some nights you tear the page out. Toledo 24, UMass 0 at the Glass Bowl on Wednesday night, and the Minutemen are 5-5. I watched every snap, and I'm going to tell you about the good parts, because there were some.

The second half was ours. Toledo scored zero points after halftime. The Rockets had six possessions in the second half, and our defense answered with four punts, a stop on fourth down and a clock that ran out. That's how you play in November.

Timmy Hinspeter was everywhere: 12 tackles, one of them for a loss. Kendall Bournes added eight, Tyler Martin had five, and Joshua Nobles made a tackle for loss of his own. That group didn't hang its head once.

The first half was the problem. Connor Walendzak broke a 69-yard run, Reice Griffith kicked a 27-yarder, and then Nicholas Thompson intercepted Logan Inagawa and returned it 62 yards. Walendzak caught a 17-yard score before the break, and it was 24-0 at halftime.

Inagawa kept swinging. He ran for 40 yards, including an 18-yarder, and Reece Adkins caught five balls for 33 yards. Drew Alsup had a 19-yard grab. Our best march went 11 plays and 53 yards late in the third quarter, and it ended on fourth down. So close to the board I could taste it.

Toledo held us to 188 yards, we converted 3 of 15 third downs, and we drew five flags for 50 yards. Not good enough, and everybody in maroon knows it. The good news is the defense gave us a blueprint for the second half of every game left.

We're 5-5 with Akron coming to Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at 7:00 PM ET. Home cooking in Amherst. Let's go get one, Minutemen.

articles.text:

Julian Fox had eight tackles, three of them for a loss. Andrew Zock had two sacks and three tackles for loss. Donovan Watkins broke up two throws. That's a shutout earned snap by snap.

articles.title: Ball State vs Buffalo: A Blocked Punt, Three Missed Kicks and a Long Night in Muncie
articles.byline: Gus Ponder, The Ball State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bulls (7-3) 28, Ball State Cardinals (3-7) 7, Wed., Nov. 11, Scheumann Stadium, Muncie. Next: at Ohio, Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Peden Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
I'll say it first so nobody else has to. Buffalo 28, Ball State 7 at Scheumann Stadium on Wednesday night, and the Cardinals are 3-7. I've sat in these seats through rough ones, but this one stings, because we had our chances.

And it opened like a dream. Late in the first quarter our special teams got a hand on a Buffalo punt, and Gabe Aramboles recovered it in the end zone. 7-0, and the home crowd of 6,745 was loud.

Then came the kicks. Brody Boehm tried from 47, 44 and 39 yards, and none of them went through. That's nine points we left on the field in a game that was tied 7-7 at the half.

The effort was there. Donovan Hamilton was a workhorse with 11 catches for 104 yards. Keldric Luster threw it 39 times and kept firing. TJ Horton ran 11 times for 92 yards. We gained 325 yards, Buffalo gained 350, and the scoreboard still said what it said.

The fourth quarter opened with our best drive of the night, nine plays and 75 yards, and it died on fourth down at the Buffalo 22. Then Messiah Burch went 67 yards, Buffalo recovered an onside kick, and Terrance Shelton Jr. went 29 more. Burch finished with 209 yards on 31 carries. Tip of the cap. Reluctantly.

Our defense hung in for three quarters. Sterling Smith had 10 tackles, Jared Badie had two sacks, and Mikeah Webster added another. Buffalo completed five throws all night for 48 yards. Keep that Bulls quarterback in the pocket and we can play with anybody in this league.

Next: at Ohio, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, at Peden Stadium in Athens. Practice those kicks, Cardinals. Put three of them through and this one looks a whole lot different. I'll be in Athens either way, loud as ever.

articles.text:
Pack a lunch, Muncie. Buffalo 28, Ball State 7 on Wednesday night at Scheumann Stadium, and the Bulls are 7-3 and 5-1 in the MAC. We ran the ball 52 times for 302 yards. I counted every carry from the visitors' side, and my mittens are done for the season.

The night opened crooked. Ball State blocked one of our punts late in the first quarter, and Gabe Aramboles fell on it in the end zone. 7-0 Cardinals. Fine. We do our best work from behind.

Jason Wright answered with an 11-play, 80-yard drive in the second quarter and finished it with a 14-yard throw to Chance Morrow. 7-7. Wright completed five throws all night, and he didn't need more. This team knows exactly who it is.

Who it is, mostly, is Messiah Burch. He carried 31 times for 209 yards and two scores. His 2-yard run capped a 12-play, 79-yard drive in the third for a 14-7 lead. Then, with 4:04 left, he found a crease up the middle and went 67 yards. 21-7.

And then the coaches got bold. Oliver Hautanen popped an onside kick, we came up with it at the Ball State 29, and Terrance Shelton Jr. went 29 yards on the very next snap. Two touchdowns in six seconds of game clock. 28-7. Shelton finished with 92 yards on 10 carries.

The defense deserves its own parade down Main Street. Ball State came away empty on fourth down three times, twice inside our 25 in the fourth quarter, and three Cardinals field goal tries, from 47, 44 and 39 yards, did not go through. SaVeon Brown and Zach Bergmann had nine tackles each, Mikey Crawford had eight, and Miles Greer chipped in a tackle for loss. Zero turnovers for us, too.

Next up is Central Michigan at Broadview Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at 7:30 PM ET. Bring the hand warmers. We're bringing the run game.

articles.title: Sacramento State vs Central Michigan: Isaiah Ene's 37-Yard Dash and a Long Night in Mount Pleasant
articles.matchup: Final: Sacramento State Hornets (2-9) 7, Central Michigan Chippewas (5-5) 28, Wed., Nov. 11, Mount Pleasant. Next: at Hawai'i, Sat., Nov. 28, 11:00 PM ET, Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, Honolulu
articles.text:
A long way from home, on a Wednesday night in Michigan, the Hornets took the field and swung. Central Michigan 28, Sacramento State 7. We're 2-9. I'm still wearing the green and gold, and I'm not taking it off.

The first drive looked like us. Brian Salazar Jr. moved the ball 66 yards in 10 plays, all the way to the Central Michigan 16, and then Justin Taylor intercepted a throw at the 7. Heartbreaker. Points there and this is a different night.

Isaiah Ene was the bright spot. Second quarter, four plays and 68 yards, and Ene went the last 37 himself to tie it 7-7. He finished with 67 yards on eight carries and caught two balls. Give that man the ball more. I'm begging.

The defense worked all night long. Leki Holani made 14 tackles. Boogsie Silvera had 11 and forced a fumble that Miles Tucker recovered at our 38. Tim Thomas added nine tackles, a tackle for loss and two hurries. Those guys never quit.

But Central Michigan had the ball for 39:48 and ran it 56 times. Vaughn Blue scored with 19 seconds left in the half, Brock Townsend broke a 40-yarder in the third, and Townsend added a late one. We finished with 211 yards and 10 first downs, and that's the whole story.

Onterrio Smith Jr. led us with four catches for 47 yards, including a 25-yarder, and Davion Godley ripped off a 23-yard run. There's talent on this roster. Ask anybody who stuck around to the end. Salazar took his hits and kept getting up, and that matters to me more than any stat sheet.

Now we get a breather, then one more trip west: at Hawai'i, Saturday, Nov. 28, 11:00 PM ET, at the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex in Honolulu. Long flight. Let's finish strong, Hornets.

articles.matchup: Final: Ohio Bobcats (7-3) 17, Miami (OH) RedHawks (6-4) 34, Tue., Nov. 10, Yager Stadium, Oxford. Next: vs Ball State, Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Peden Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
I'm going to say it once and then talk football. Ohio led Miami 17-0 in the second quarter on Tuesday night at Yager Stadium and lost the Battle of the Bricks 34-17. The six-game winning streak is done. The perfect MAC record is done. We're 7-3 and 5-1, and it's a quiet ride back to Athens.

The first quarter and a half looked like the team I love. Nick Poulos took us 75 yards in eight plays on the opening drive and hit Riley Neer for an 8-yard touchdown. Duncan Brune punched one in from the 1 early in the second quarter. Brack Peacock added a 22-yarder. Michael Molnar was living in their backfield, with a sack and 8 tackles on the night.

Then it slipped. Miami's freshman receiver Scoop Smith threw a 15-yard touchdown with 1:02 left in the half. We still drove to the Miami 18 in the final minute. Peacock's 34-yarder at the gun missed, a Miami flag gave us one more snap from the 8, and the throw from our holder was knocked down. Zero points from the 8. I would have kicked it again.

Second half: zero points. We converted 3 of 17 third downs for the game, and we had seven penalties for 44 yards, several of them flags before the snap. You can't move the chains walking backward.

And the ending. Down 20-17 with 3:55 left, we were moving, and Poulos fumbled at our own 48. Malcolm McCain took it away. D'Shawntae Jones went 48 yards on the next play. Then Amariyun Knighten intercepted Poulos and took it back 58 yards. Miami scored 20 points in the fourth quarter.

Credit where it's due. Poulos ran 17 times for 68 yards and threw for 193, Neer caught 6 balls for 74 and the touchdown, and Darren James-Hamilton and Molnar each had 8 tackles. Our defense held Miami to 10 completions in 25 tries. The giveaways beat us, not the effort.

Ohio Athletics said we came to Oxford looking for a third straight win in this series. That'll have to wait a year. Ball State comes to Peden Stadium next Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 7:00 PM ET. Hold onto the football, and the MAC race is still right in front of us.

articles.byline: Cordelia Van Doren, The Miami (OH) Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Ohio Bobcats (7-3) 17, Miami (OH) RedHawks (6-4) 34, Tue., Nov. 10, Yager Stadium, Oxford. Next: at Kent State, Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium, Kent
articles.text:
Down 17-0. At home. On Senior Night. In the Battle of the Bricks. Then the RedHawks scored the last 34 points of the night, and Miami beat Ohio 34-17 at Yager Stadium. We're 6-4 and 4-2 in the MAC, and Miami Athletics said before the game that a win would make us bowl eligible again. Done.

The turn came with 1:02 left in the first half, and it came from a receiver. Scoop Smith, the freshman, took the ball and threw 15 yards to Maleek Huggins for a touchdown. 17-7. Drew Bellisari had come in at quarterback on that drive and hit Braylon Isom twice to get us there.

Ohio still had one more chance before the break. Brack Peacock missed from 34 at the gun, our unsportsmanlike flag gave them one more snap from the 8, and they tried a throw from the holder. Blayne Myrick knocked it down. Halftime, and you could feel it turning.

Our defense pitched a shutout in the second half. Ohio converted 3 of 17 third downs all night. Bellisari ran 31 yards to the 1 to set up D'Shawntae Jones's touchdown, Brady Stidham tied it from 36 early in the fourth, and Bellisari broke a 26-yarder that set up Stidham's 25-yarder for a 20-17 lead with 3:55 left.

And then the last two minutes, which I would like framed. Malcolm McCain forced a Nick Poulos fumble and recovered it himself at the Ohio 48. Next snap, Jones went 48 yards for the touchdown. Twenty seconds later, Amariyun Knighten intercepted Poulos and returned it 58 yards for another. Yager came apart at the seams.

Jones finished with 115 yards and two touchdowns on 18 carries, a week after he ran for 112 against Buffalo. McCain had 12 tackles, CJ Young had 11, and Roosevelt Andrews III had a sack. Seniors, that's how you say goodbye to Yager.

Ohio came in on a six-game winning streak with a perfect MAC record, and The Miami Student reminded everyone that the Bobcats had won the last two meetings. Ask them how Oxford was.

Next Tuesday, Nov. 17, we're at Kent State, 7:00 PM ET at Dix Stadium.

articles.title: Kent State vs Bowling Green: A Fourth-Quarter Comeback That Lasted Nine Seconds
articles.byline: Ozzie Brannigan, The Kent State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Kent State Golden Flashes (3-7) 28, Bowling Green Falcons (3-7) 33, Tue., Nov. 10, Doyt L. Perry Stadium, Bowling Green. Next: vs Miami (OH), Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium, Kent
articles.text:
I expected the worst. I got a more creative version. Kent State came back from 13 points down in the fourth quarter at Doyt L. Perry Stadium, took a 28-27 lead with 2:00 left, and lost 33-28 anyway. The lead lasted nine seconds. We're 3-7, 2-4 in the MAC, and the Anniversary Award rides back to Bowling Green.

Let me be fair, because Dru DeShields earned it. He threw for 332 yards and two touchdowns and ran for two more, including the 25-yard run that put us ahead. I was on my feet. I don't stand up for much.

Wayne Harris was the best player on the field. Eight catches, 143 yards, a 39-yard score in the second quarter for a 14-7 lead and a 13-yarder in the fourth to begin the comeback. Da'Realyst Clark added 107 yards on five catches. Those two can play with anybody in this conference.

Here's where my mood went. Early in the fourth we drove 67 yards, and DeShields was intercepted by Josira Andrews at the Bowling Green 2. Points, gone. Then there's Myles Bradley, who ESPN credits with five sacks against us. Five. We converted 5 of 17 third downs. You can't live like that.

After our go-ahead score, Bowling Green needed two plays: a 16-yard catch by Joseph Saffold and a 48-yard run by Nakai Amachree. We stopped the two-point try, which I mention only because I like to be accurate. Then DeShields got us to the Bowling Green 35, took a sack, and threw it into the end zone, where Nick Sawyer caught it. Touchback. That's the season in one sentence.

Some good news, since I'm required to look for it. Jaihien Roy had a sack and 6 tackles, Darian Blachewicz had a sack and a half, and Hayden Dawahare made 9 tackles. The defense held Bowling Green to 118 rushing yards and 6 of 14 on third down.

Next Tuesday, Nov. 17, Miami (OH) comes to Dix Stadium for a 7:00 PM ET kickoff. We haven't won on the road this year, so a home game is welcome news. I expect rain. I expect it every week.

articles.title: Akron vs Western Michigan: Marcel Williams Bounces Back Twice in a 42-14 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Western Michigan Broncos (7-3) 42, Akron Zips (1-9) 14, Tue., Nov. 10, InfoCision Stadium, Akron. Next: at Massachusetts, Wed., Nov. 18, 7:00 PM ET, Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium, Amherst
articles.text:
I'm not going to dress this one up. Western Michigan came into InfoCision Stadium on the eve of Veterans Day and ran the ball right through us for 360 yards. Final score, Western Michigan 42, Akron 14. We're 1-9 and 0-6 in the MAC, and I still showed up early with my flag pin on.

Here's the figure that hurts most: 42:46. That's how long the Broncos held the football. We had it for 17:14. You can't win a game you're watching from the bench. They converted 13 of 17 third downs, and Cole Cabana broke an 82-yard run early in the second quarter that I'm going to see in my sleep.

But this is the Rubber City, and rubber bounces. Cibastian Broughton answered that Cabana run three plays later, hitting Marcel Williams for 35 yards and a touchdown to make it 14-7. In the fourth quarter, same two guys, 39 yards, another score. Williams finished with 5 catches for 85 yards and both touchdowns. Broughton went 12 of 18 for 173 yards. When those two are rolling, Akron has a heartbeat.

Give it up for the defense on fourth down, too. Western Michigan went for it four times and converted once. On the very first drive, Cyrus Durham helped drop Broc Lowry for a 9-yard loss on fourth-and-1, and the Broncos had to hand it back. Tairan Davis Jr. made 15 tackles, 13 of them by himself. That man was everywhere, and he deserved more help.

Brandon Hills took seven kickoffs back for 139 yards, which tells you two facts. He's tough, and we gave up a lot of points. Jordan Gant ran 9 times for 61 yards, and I wanted to see him 20 more times.

Now the honest part. We gave up 566 yards. Jalen Buckley ran for 121 and two scores, Cabana for 107, and their two quarterbacks completed 22 of 24 throws between them. One Bronco drive went 17 plays and ate 9:19 of clock. That's not a bad night. That's a long night.

Next Wednesday, Nov. 18, it's Akron at UMass, 7:00 PM ET at McGuirk. Feed Marcel Williams early, keep our defense off the field, and let's bring one more win home to Summit County. Zip, zip, hooray.

But this is the Rubber City, and rubber bounces. Cibastian Broughton answered that Cabana run three plays later, hitting Marcel Williams for 35 yards and a touchdown to make it 14-7. In the fourth quarter, same two guys, 39 yards, another score. Williams finished with 5 catches for 85 yards and both touchdowns. Broughton went 12 of 18 for 173 yards. When those two are rolling, Akron has a heartbeat.

Give it up for the defense on fourth down, too. Western Michigan went for it four times and converted once. On the very first drive, Cyrus Durham helped drop Broc Lowry for a 9-yard loss on fourth-and-1, and the Broncos had to hand it back. Tairan Davis Jr. made 15 tackles, 13 of them by himself. That man was everywhere, and he deserved more help.

Brandon Hills took seven kickoffs back for 139 yards, which tells you two facts. He's tough, and we gave up a lot of points. Jordan Gant ran 9 times for 61 yards, and I wanted to see him 20 more times.

Now the honest part. We gave up 566 yards. Jalen Buckley ran for 121 and two scores, Cabana for 107, and their two quarterbacks completed 22 of 24 throws between them. One Bronco drive went 17 plays and ate 9:19 of clock. That's not a bad night. That's a long night.
Next Wednesday, Nov. 18, it's Akron at UMass, 7:00 PM ET at McGuirk. Feed Marcel Williams early, keep our defense off the field, and let's bring one more win home to Summit County. Zip, zip, hooray.

Cibastian Broughton threw both Akron touchdowns to Marcel Williams, from 35 and 39 yards; Williams finished with 85 receiving yards, and Tairan Davis Jr. made 15 tackles.
The Broncos needed 42 minutes of clock to beat us. We'll take that as a compliment.
